rows: Cloud networking engineer (AWS or Azure virtual networks, hybrid links)
Builds and fixes virtual networks, private links to offices, firewalls and load balancers in the cloud, often through code.
Second job for most people. Needs routing basics first, then a cloud account you have actually built in.
Scalable
Cloud networking skills sell as project work and consulting, and the same skill moves across employers.
Network security engineer (firewalls, VPN, segmentation)
Writes and reviews firewall rules, secures remote access, and checks that a change does not open a hole.
Usually after a year or two as a network engineer.
Scalable with a business layer
Firewall reviews and managed security for small firms can be sold as a service. See the security guide for the wider lane.
Enterprise network engineer (switching, routing, Wi-Fi in an office or campus)
Keeps a company's wired and wireless network running, plans upgrades, and handles outages.
Entry through support, NOC or a junior engineer post.
Scalable with a business layer
A salaried ladder with fixed grades. It grows when you add automation and design skill, or serve small offices yourself.
SD-WAN and WAN engineer at an integrator or managed service provider
Connects many branch offices, banks' outlets or stores over broadband and leased lines, and manages them from one console.
Integrators and managed service providers hire juniors who have lab proof.
Scalable with a business layer
Repeatable rollouts across many sites. Ownership comes through a small managed-service business.
